question.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z\ge -1.32).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/d89bd5f38fdf4c952146dde8cd01207167c92cab07290742d229ceb0f4cf5712.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.32) & =1-P(Z<-1.32) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.32)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/0959a3c48bf70d10f24d85cd98bcd0703db4765ba5349d02896e18104c3f98a7.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-1.32)=0.0934.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.32) & =1-Φ(-1.32) \\  & =1-0.0934 \\  & =0.9066.\end{aligned}
$$
